national_raw_news.content: President Droupadi Murmu has said that the Indian Economy is moving ahead as the fastest-growing major economy despite warfare and instability prevailing in several parts of the world. Addressing the nation on the eve of the 80th Independence Day this evening, the President highlighted that according to economic projections, the growth rate of the Indian economy is expected to be more than twice the average global growth rate. She added that ‘Atmanirbhar Bharat Abhiyan’ has further strengthened the foundation of the country’s economic progress and national security. The President highlighted that India has achieved some of the Sustainable Development Goals 2030, ahead of schedule. President Droupadi Murmu also noted that national interest is the foundation of India’s foreign policy and peace, cooperation, dialogue, and the ideal of Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam are the pillars of its foreign policy. She said, India has entered into Free Trade Agreements with many countries to enhance economic cooperation and strengthen mutual relations. The President said that India is playing a leading role among the countries of the Global South and the country has grown in stature on the global stage. President Murmu said, India believes in a rules-based international order, and her endeavour is to ensure that the global community receives appropriate representation in the United Nations and other multilateral organisations. She said, this endeavour has been getting strong support from many countries. On Operation Sindoor, President Droupadi Murmu said that the historic operation against terrorism demonstrated the capability of the Indian Armed Forces to act with precision. She said, the Operation sent a clear and firm message to terrorists and those who support them that no matter where they hide, they will have to face the consequences of their actions. She said, the suspension of the Indus Waters Treaty with the country that harbours terrorism is a decisive step in the interest of the nation, especially the farmers. President Droupadi Murmu highlighted that making the country Naxal-free is a major achievement, as for decades, Naxalism posed a serious challenge to the nation. She said, today, the areas once affected by Naxalism are filled with enthusiasm. In her address, the President said that students are the architects of India’s future and everyone must contribute to safeguard their future. As Public examinations become gateways to the opportunities for the students, she emphasised that the Government is undertaking comprehensive steps to reform these examinations. The objectives of these reforms are to completely curb the use of unfair means in public examinations, make the examination system more transparent, more secure, and more trustworthy for the youth. President Droupadi Murmu also highlighted that equality of status and of opportunity, along with the dignity of the individual, are among the cherished ideals of the Constitution. She said, today, people from ordinary backgrounds are making extraordinary contributions in many fields. In her address, the President also threw light on the upliftment of the deprived sections of society, saying that more than 25 crore people have been lifted out of poverty. She mentioned...

national_raw_news.title: 11 hours ago | National 44 India Reiterates Jammu and Kashmir, Ladakh Are Integral Parts of the Country
national_raw_news.content: New Delhi today reiterated that Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh are an inalienable and integral part of India. Briefing media in the national capital this evening, External Affairs Ministry spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said, the issues that should concern the international community are the atrocities currently being perpetrated in Pakistan-occupied Jammu and Kashmir, and the use of PoJK for cross-border terrorism. Replying to a question, Mr Jaiswal stated that India has had several engagements with Afghanistan in the last few months. He highlighted that there have been several Ministerial visits from Afghanistan to India, which have led to the strengthening of partnership in areas including development, cooperation, trade, and connectivity. He added that India has long-standing ties with Afghanistan, and it looks forward to further strengthening these ties. On Bangladesh requesting additional diesel supplies from India amid energy crisis, Mr Jaiswal said, India has an ongoing arrangement with Bangladesh for the supply of diesel. He added that the additional request for diesel will be examined keeping in mind India’s own requirements, refining capacity, as well as the availability of diesel in the country. Replying to another query, the spokesperson said, India has extended an invitation to Prime Minister of Bangladesh, Tarique Rahman for a bilateral visit. India has also extended an invitation to the Bangladesh PM for a visit to India for the outreach session of the BRICS Summit. On FCRA, the spokesperson reiterated that legislative matters concerning India are internal matters on which Parliament will decide. On Russian President Vladimir Putin’s statement that India is showing growing interest in Russia’s Northern Sea Route, the spokesperson pointed out that India has a multi-faceted cooperation with Russia and connectivity is an important part of this. Mr Jaiswal conveyed deepest condolences on the lives that have been lost due to the earthquake in Colombia. He said, India sent 20 metric tons of relief material to the country today, which includes medical supplies, medical equipment, and several other items that are helpful for post-earthquake recovery.

national_raw_news.title: Delhi court allows CBI to conduct further investigation in NEET-UG paper leak case
national_raw_news.content: The Special Fast Track Court in Delhi has allowed the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) to conduct further investigation in the NEET UG Paper leak case, as new evidence has surfaced during the investigation. The CBI sought permission to keep open the investigation into other conspirators in the NEET UG Paper leak case, other than 13 accused persons against whom a charge sheet has already been filed. Special Judge Ajay Gupta allowed the application of the CBI and said that it is well settled law that further investigation can be carried out even after commencement of trial. In its letter, the CBI stated that after analysing CFSL reports, certain digital evidence has surfaced due to which it has become necessary to obtain further expert opinions. It was also stated that some more digital devices, seized during investigation, are being sent to CFSL, and the reports of which shall be filed, as and when received. The CBI said that further investigation with regard to the involvement of other conspirators is continuing and upon completion of the same, a supplementary charge-sheet will be filed.

national_raw_news.title: NTA to release provisional answer keys for UGC-NET, CSIR-NET and ICAR-NET 2026
national_raw_news.content: The National Testing Agency (NTA) has announced that the provisional answer keys for UGC-NET, CSIR-NET and ICAR AIEEA (PG) and AICE (PhD) 2026 will be published tomorrow. The NTA advised candidates to rely only on official communications from the agency regarding the examinations and answer keys. The computer-based examination, held across 87 subjects, determines eligibility for the Junior Research Fellowship (JRF), appointment as Assistant Professor, and admission to PhD programmes in universities across the country. Earlier, the Jawaharlal Nehru University Students’ Union (JNUSU) wrote to the University Grants Commission (UGC) and the NTA expressing “deep concern” over the delay in releasing the provisional answer key and final results.

national_raw_news.title: FM Nirmala Sitharaman says PM Internship Scheme aims to bridge industry-skill gap
national_raw_news.content: Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman has said that the Prime Minister Internship Scheme (PMIS) has been designed to help bridge the gap between industry expectations and the skills of candidates who apply for jobs under the scheme. Interacting with the interns in New Delhi, Mrs Sitharaman said the scheme has been designed after interactions with industry people as well as graduates and those who completed ITI courses. Under the PMIS, implemented by the Ministry of Corporate Affairs, those in the 18-25 age group are eligible to join and the interns receive a minimum financial assistance of 9,000 rupees per month. The third round of the pilot phase of the scheme is underway. The Minister said the scheme is helping bridge this gap by providing young people with hands-on industry experience. She said the scheme also enables the youth to pursue internship opportunities in areas of interest and the candidates will be able to get additional skills beyond their qualifications.

national_raw_news.title: Romania Begins Shutdown of Second Cernavoda Nuclear Reactor Amid Severe Drought
national_raw_news.content: Romania has begun a controlled shutdown of the second reactor at its Cernavoda nuclear power plant as severe drought continues to affect much of Europe. Plant operator Nuclearelectrica said scorching temperatures and weeks of below-average rainfall have pushed the Danube River to record-low levels. The conditions forced the plant to shut down its first reactor in late July this year. The plant accounts for around 20 per cent of Romania’s electricity generation when operating at full capacity. Meanwhile, the country’s Ministry of Energy has said the country’s electricity needs can be met through alternative sources and imports following the shutdown of the second reactor.

national_raw_news.title: Eight Killed in Suspected Gas Leak at Shipbreaking Yard in Bangladesh
national_raw_news.content: Eight people were killed in a suspected gas leak at a shipbreaking yard in Bangladesh today. Police said, the incident occurred at the Ferdous Steel Ship Breaking Yard in the Sitakunda area, during the dismantling of a decommissioned ship. Several other workers were injured in the incident. Police said, the initial death toll was six, but two more workers succumbed to their injuries after being taken from the site. Officials said, the workers died due to toxic gas emissions from the ship. Authorities are investigating the cause of the gas leak and whether adequate safety measures were in place for the workers at the yard.

national_raw_news.title: Two UAE vessels attacked while transiting Strait of Hormuz
national_raw_news.content: Two vessels of the United Arab Emirates were attacked while transiting the Strait of Hormuz last evening. In a statement posted on social media, the UAE Ministry of Foreign Affairs condemned the Iranian attacks, stressing the necessity for Iran to cease attacks. The Ministry of Foreign Affairs noted that this attack constitutes a flagrant violation of UN Security Council resolution 2817, which affirmed the importance of freedom of navigation, and rejected the targeting of commercial vessels or the obstruction of international maritime routes. The Ministry stressed that targeting commercial shipping and using the Strait of Hormuz as a tool of economic coercion or blackmail represents acts of piracy by Iran’s Revolutionary Guard Corps and constitutes a direct threat to the stability of the region, its peoples, and global energy security.

national_raw_news.title: Sinquefield Cup 2026: Praggnanandhaa Makes Strong Comeback, Defeats Van Foreest 14 Aug 2026 | 7:28 PM 86
national_raw_news.content: Indian Grandmaster R. Praggnanandhaa bounced back from his previous-round defeat to secure a convincing victory over Dutch player Jorden Van Foreest in the fourth round of the Sinquefield Cup. The win took Praggnanandhaa’s tally to two-and-a-half points from four games, placing him in a share of second position in the 10-player, nine-round tournament. Praggnanandhaa had suffered a defeat against Germany’s Vincent Keymer in the previous round. His latest victory will boost his confidence and strengthen his bid for a podium finish. The Sinquefield Cup is part of the Grand Chess Tour, with a strong performance in the tournament also crucial for players seeking qualification for the Grand Chess Tour finale.

national_raw_news.title: Iga Swiatek beats Elena Rybakina to claim Women’s Singles title at Canadian Open Tennis 14 Aug 2026 | 8:30 AM 368
national_raw_news.content: In Canadian Open Tennis, seventh seed Iga Swiatek of Poland defeated second seed Elena Rybakina in straight sets to claim the Women’s Singles title in Toronto last night. Swiatek captured her first title of the season with a swift 6-2 6-3 win, giving her a confidence boost heading into the US Open. In Men’s Singles, American tennis player Ben Shelton won the title in Montreal by defeating fellow American Brandon Nakashima with a score of 6-3, 7-6(4). With this victory, the fifth-seeded Shelton successfully defended his tournament crown and captured his second career ATP Masters 1000 trophy. This victory marks his fourth tournament win of the 2026 season, following earlier titles in Dallas, Munich, and Stuttgart, bringing his total career tour-level titles to seven.

national_raw_news.title: Commonwealth Fencing: Indian team dominates with 35 medals comprising 13 gold 13 Aug 2026 | 8:30 PM 881
national_raw_news.content: India emerged as the overall champions at the Commonwealth Fencing Championship by winning an impressive 35 medals after four days of competition held at Lagos in Nigeria. Indian contingent secured thirteen gold, eight silver, and fourteen bronze medals at the event across the Under 23 and senior competitions. The senior Indian fencers claimed five gold medals in six events on the fourth and final day of the competition, securing honours in Men’s Sabre, Women’s Sabre, Men’s E’pée, Women’s Epée and Women’s foil, as well as a silver in Men’s foil. The performance also helped India win the Wilkinson Sword Trophy, awarded by the Commonwealth Fencing Federation to the country with the best overall results. Secretary-general, Fencing Association of India, Rajeev Mehta, said in a statement that lifting the Commonwealth Overall Championship title for the first time is a testament to the talent, discipline, and hard work within Indian fencing.

national_raw_news.title: Canadian Open Tennis: Men’s and women’s semifinals locked in 13 Aug 2026 | 6:37 PM 539
national_raw_news.content: In Canadian Open Tennis, second seed Elena Rybakina will take on seventh seed Iga Swiatek in Women’s Singles title clash at Toronto tomorrow. Kazakhstan’s Rybakina defeated fourth seeded American Coco Gauff by 5-7,6-2,6-2 while Polish player Swiatek overpowered Elina Svitolina of Ukraine by 6-3,1-6, 6-3 in the semi-finals today. In Men’s Singles, defending champion Ben Shelton will face Brandon Nakashima in an All American final at Montreal tomorrow. Fifth seed Shelton secured a 6-2, 6-3 victory over fellow American and 12th seed Learner Tien while 28th seed Nakashima beat Spanish teenager and 20th seed Rafael Jodar 7-6(3) 6-4 to reach his first Masters 1000 final.

national_raw_news.title: Country’s exports register robust growth of over 13% in July 13 Aug 2026 | 8:45 PM 286
national_raw_news.content: The country’s total exports, including merchandise and services are estimated at 80.14 billion US dollars in July this year, registering a robust 13.3 per cent year-on-year growth. According to the provisional data released by the Commerce Ministry, the export performance was led by merchandise shipments, which jumped over 19.6 per cent to 44.24 billion US dollars from a year earlier. The growth in merchandise exports was driven by petroleum products, electronic goods, engineering goods, organic and inorganic chemicals, cotton yarn and handloom products. Country’s merchandise trade deficit widened by 31.5 per cent year-on-year to 15 billion US dollars last month. Cumulatively, merchandise exports during April to July period of the current financial year are estimated at 173.78 billion US dollars, registering an increase of 17 per cent on an annual basis.

national_raw_news.title: Asian markets in gain, and European indices show mixed response 13 Aug 2026 | 5:45 PM 311
national_raw_news.content: In the Asian markets, South Korea’s Kospi index gained almost 3.6 per cent and Japan’s Nikkei 225 rose around 1.2 per cent. Among the major European indices, Germany’s DAX was trading 0.4 per cent up, while London’s FTSE 100 dropped 0.3 per cent, when reports last came in. On economic front, United Kingdom’s real gross domestic product (GDP) is estimated to have increased by 0.4 per cent in April to June quarter of this year, down from growth of 0.6 per cent in the first quarter. Meanwhile, GDP grew by 0.3 per cent in June, after registering no growth in the previous month, according to the GDP figures released today by the Office for National Statistics.
